strengths: Clearly contrasts the sulfur dioxide cap-and-trading mechanism with the nitrogen oxides rate-based approach.
Preserves useful qualifications, including the scope of the nitrogen oxides rules and the distinction between units and plants.
Includes concrete coverage figures and a later cap milestone.
weaknesses: The handoff describes how the rules differed, but does not explain why the program used two rules, as the title promises.
The progression mixes the pollutant timelines; “Its phase I” is ambiguous after the nitrogen oxides sentence.
redundancy: Low in the handoff itself; evidence records largely repeat its claims.
peripheralDetail: The sulfur dioxide coverage counts and 2010 cap are useful timeline evidence, but less directly serve the central comparison.
usability: Usable after clarifying which pollutant the phase I milestones describe and aligning the title with the evidence.
defects: No supported explanation for why the program adopted different rules.
Ambiguous “Its” makes the phase I date and coverage figures easy to attribute to the wrong pollutant.
